title: Understanding product use after release
subtitle: Usage, feedback & follow-up.
description: Feature-adoption analysis and friction monitoring: from planned instrumentation and production data to user feedback, follow-up work and continued observation.
summary: At TrustPointAI, I combine adoption analysis with friction monitoring to understand how a released feature works for users and what needs to change.

card.title: Understanding product use after release
card.summary: I connect usage data and user feedback to guide product improvements, including the move to left navigation. I also built a workflow that turns Datadog frustration signals into assigned follow-up work.

signals.note: Datadog rage clicks, dead clicks and error clicks provide starting points for investigation. They need context before they can explain a usability problem.

branches.label: Act
branches.title: Clear error
branches.text: Create a ticket automatically and assign responsibility using context and feature ownership in the codebase.

branches.label: Assess
branches.title: Needs judgment
branches.text: Bring the finding to discussion. A person evaluates it before a ticket is created and assigned.

branches.label: Observe
branches.title: Below the attention threshold
branches.text: Keep the finding in the history for trend analysis without requiring immediate attention.

items.title: Understand feature adoption
items.text: I build dashboards using production database and Datadog data. The events needed for analysis are planned and implemented during development, making it possible to examine adoption and user choices after release.

example.title: From top navigation to a left sidebar
example.intro: We introduced left navigation with an option to return to the previous top navigation. Because this was a substantial interface change, we followed the transition over an extended period.

steps.title: Observe the transition
steps.text: We tracked who switched to the new navigation and who returned to the old one. I also examined how screen size related to that choice.

steps.title: Ask about the experience
steps.text: Users who returned to the old navigation received a Refiner survey asking what did not work for them in the new approach.

steps.title: Improve before the full rollout
steps.text: The team made improvements based on the feedback, then moved all users to the left-navigation experience.

items.title: Investigate friction and decide what needs action
items.text: I built an automation that analyzes and groups Datadog frustration signals, then routes findings to action, human assessment or continued observation.
items.supporting: A person reviews and confirms selected tickets before sending them to an AI agent for fixes.

items.title: Follow through after a change
items.text: Previously identified and fixed signals stay in the monitoring history. The automation checks them every day for recurrence and trends.
items.supporting: Earlier findings remain part of the analysis, even when the latest run is quiet.

outcome.text: Usage analysis and feedback informed navigation improvements before the team moved all users to the left sidebar. The frustration-signal workflow adds assigned follow-up work and daily checks for recurring issues.

technical.title: Technical details
technical.text: Production queries and instrumented events supply adoption dashboards; Refiner adds targeted feedback. Ticket assignment uses feature ownership in the codebase, and monitoring retains findings across runs.
technical.stack: Event instrumentation · Database analysis · Datadog · Refiner · Engineering automation
